gaps.note: Cut from Kevin's reaction to Daymond and Lori's reaction hides intermediate panel responses.
Cut after Lori exits hides the transition to Peter's questioning.
Cut from Justin accepting the deal to Mark clapping hides the immediate reaction.

stage_a.note: The founder maintains a confident, upbeat delivery with frequent smiles while explaining the product.
The founder shows strong engagement when demonstrating the problem with traditional dress shirts.
The founder opens with a friendly, approachable demeanor and maintains eye contact with the panel.

venture.description: A comfortable polo shirt with a firm dress collar designed to be worn under sweaters or jackets.
venture.note: The product aims to solve the discomfort of wearing a full dress shirt under a sweater.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder introduces himself, states his ask, explains the discomfort of traditional dress shirts, and presents his dress collar polo solution.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond notes the product samples in front of the panel.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin examines the shirt sample he received.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori comments on the nice, stretchy material of the shirt.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms the material is stretchy and lightweight.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori adds that the material is totally breathable.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks the founder to confirm that he offered four percent equity.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms the four percent equity offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter acknowledges the confirmation of the equity offer.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks what the sales have been so far.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states they started last year and have sold ninety-two thousand shirts for five point four million dollars.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond reacts with surprise to the high sales figures.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori also reacts positively to the sales numbers.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if the sales are direct to consumer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms that all sales are direct to consumer and online.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks what the profit margin was on the sales.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states a net profit margin of twenty percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark expresses that the profit margin is impressive.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond compliments the product, saying it is really well made.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Daymond for the compliment.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond explains he hates the Midtown look and hates offers of four percent, so he exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark laughs at Daymond's swift and blunt exit.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin points out that rapid growth requires execution skills and asks what specific skills the founder has.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder agrees and explains that their secret weapon is their marketing funnel.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks what the founder was doing for the previous twenty years.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states he was in internet marketing and ran a business doing check-in applications for events.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori praises the product but decides it is not the right investment for her and exits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder thanks Lori for her feedback.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter mentions his experience with global brands in Asia and asks for the manufacturing cost.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains the landed cost is fifteen dollars and the retail price is sixty-five to seventy-five dollars.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin notes he has never bid on a shirt deal before but offers three hundred thousand dollars for ten percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder immediately rejects Kevin's ten percent offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark jokes about Kevin being decisive.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder argues that his business is a fast-growing DTC brand, not a slow-growth private equity deal.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark points out that the founder will eventually hit a wall in growth.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks if the founder has any other investors.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms he has no other investors and is the sole owner.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter criticizes the founder for completely dismissing an offer that he considered to be pretty good.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond asks what sort of equity the founder is actually willing to discuss.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter reiterates that the founder dismissed Kevin's offer as if he wasn't even in the room.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter points out that ten percent implies a three million dollar valuation, questioning the founder's higher expectations.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder asserts that the business is not worth seven and a half million, but rather twenty million.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter asks the founder to justify why the company is worth twenty million.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin interrupts to ask what the company's free EBITDA is.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states a twenty percent margin, making one million dollars on five million in sales.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks the founder what he actually needs the money for.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder explains he needs funds for inventory, marketing, and building a team to reach fifty million.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark asks if he is looking to raise equity or find a line of credit for the inventory.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder confirms he needs a line of credit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states he is also looking for a mentor to help him grow the business to the next level.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond sarcastically offers to mentor him if he takes Kevin's ten percent offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder ignores the sarcasm and insists his company could be the next great brand.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter warns that the fashion market is brutal and shifts rapidly, suggesting the product could go out of fashion quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder disagrees, asserting his belief that the product is not going out of fashion.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond argues that a looming recession will reduce shirt purchases, causing inventory to eat into profits.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder counters that their core styles are timeless and will last for thirty years.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond cites Levi's declining sales to prove that everything eventually goes out of style.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter announces that he is about to make an offer.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori advises the founder to listen to Peter.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter offers his infrastructure to cut costs and proposes three hundred thousand dollars for ten percent.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond questions why the founder is engaging with Peter when he previously rejected the same terms from Kevin.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reiterates his objection to the three million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond points out that the founder was already lowering his valuation expectation.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder questions why Daymond assumes he would drop his valuation so low.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark notes that three hundred thousand isn't enough and asks where the founder will get additional capital.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder states he probably needs a seven hundred thousand dollar line of credit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark joins Peter's offer, adding a seven hundred thousand dollar line of credit at market interest rates.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder jokingly calls Mark a tough negotiator.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark questions why offering a line of credit makes him a tough negotiator.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder points out that they have hard assets and inventory to back a line of credit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark notes that clothing inventory is notoriously difficult to get a line of credit against.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori urges the founder to listen to Mark and Peter, highlighting their extensive backgrounds.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark invites the founder to make them a counter offer.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond expresses frustration, asking if they are just wasting time.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder complains again that they are valuing his company at only three million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond pressures the founder to make his counter offer quickly.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder counters with five percent equity for the three hundred thousand cash and the line of credit.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark shakes his head, silently rejecting the five percent counter offer.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin reacts with surprise to the low counter offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder insists that giving up ten percent is just too much.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin withdraws his standing offer and exits the negotiation, citing the founder's refusal of ten percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter tells the founder he has done well just to get a ten percent offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder challenges Peter again on the three million dollar valuation.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter argues that the valuation is about the incremental growth they will bring.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter criticizes the founder for not listening, saying a partnership requires two ears.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder defends himself, claiming he is listening.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter insists the founder is talking over him and not allowing him to voice his opinion.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder reassures Peter that he hears what he is saying.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter argues that the founder is discounting the immense value they add for a mere six percent difference.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder denies that he is discounting the value the investors bring.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori chimes in, suggesting that with Mark and Peter, the business could reach eighty million.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond reminds the founder that the investors' lives will not change if they don't do the deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter agrees with Daymond, reinforcing that they don't need this deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter emphasizes that there is no amount of money the founder could pay to hire him and Mark.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder stubbornly asks again if they wouldn't give a discount on the valuation.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark expresses doubt that a deal will happen and exits the negotiation.

turns.speaker: S2
turns.summary: Lori observes that all the investors appear to be out.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder desperately asks Mark if he would do the deal for seven percent.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark firmly says no to the seven percent offer.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder turns to Peter and officially counters with seven percent.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter confirms that he is also out, rejecting the seven percent.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder repeats his seven percent offer, hoping for a change of heart.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter repeats that they are out.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter tells the founder that he will regret this moment one day.

turns.speaker: S3
turns.summary: Daymond points out that the founder still has a chance to say yes to the ten percent.

turns.speaker: S5
turns.summary: Kevin re-enters the negotiation by offering the exact terms Mark and Peter had: ten percent and the line of credit.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder ignores Kevin and asks Peter if he is still in for the ten percent deal.

turns.speaker: S1
turns.summary: Peter decides to re-enter and confirms he is still in.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder turns to Mark and asks for a yes or no.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark nods silently, indicating his re-entry into the deal.

turns.speaker: F1
turns.summary: The founder accepts Mark and Peter's offer.

turns.speaker: S4
turns.summary: Mark claps and expresses satisfaction that the deal is done.

decisions.note: Hates the look of the product and hates offers of 4% equity.
Likes the product but feels it is not the right investment for her.

decisions.terms: My offer is also at 10% for $300,000.
decisions.note: Offers $300k for 10% equity, adding his infrastructure value.

decisions.terms: If I went in with Peter... I don't mind putting up a line of credit of 700,000 dollars.
decisions.note: Joins Peter's offer, adding the requested $700k line of credit at market interest.
Counters Mark and Peter's offer with 5% equity instead of 10%.
Withdraws his offer and exits because the founder thinks 10% is too much.
Exits because he feels the founder is too stubborn on valuation.
Counters with 7% equity after Mark exits.

decisions.terms: We're all out, right? We're all out.
decisions.note: Rejects the 7% counter and confirms his exit.

decisions.terms: 300,000 dollars in equity for 10%. I'll put up a line of credit of 700,000 dollars.
decisions.note: Re-enters with the same terms Mark and Peter had offered.
Re-enters his previous offer of $300k and LOC for 10% after the founder asks him.
Non-verbally confirms his re-entry into the deal with Peter.
Accepts Mark and Peter's offer of $300k and a $700k line of credit for 10% equity.

record.notes: Mark Cuban's re-entry at 10:37 is a silent nod, recorded as a decides turn.
